title: A minimal authorization-server document advertises none of the three properties
rationale: The negative case for the three descriptive checks, and it is deliberately labelled `undecidable` rather than `violating`. None of the three can report a failure -- `CheckResult.model_post_init` raises for a DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY check that does, and `test_only_failable_checks_are_claimed_as_violated` refuses a fixture that claims otherwise -- because in each case the absent member is permitted: RFC 9207 2.3's MUST is conditional on supporting the parameter, RFC 9728 4 marks `protected_resources` OPTIONAL, and no rung of MCP's registration ladder is mandatory. So what the instrument must produce here is UNSPECIFIED, and a pack that only contained the positive case would not distinguish "absent" from "present" at all. This document is not a strawman: the GitHub Actions OIDC document captured in `control-github-actions-real-deployment` has exactly this shape.

spec.quote: authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: Boolean parameter indicating whether the authorization server provides the iss parameter in the authorization response as defined in Section 2. If omitted, the default value is false.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 30 July 2026. The default is what makes absence measurable rather than merely unknown: a conforming client must treat the omission as "not supported".

spec.quote:
protected_resources
      OPTIONAL.  JSON array containing a list of resource identifiers for OAuth protected resources that can be used with this authorization server.
